Problem 752. Position chain from Dover to Linden
Knowledge context.
A map can be modeled with relative positions. When several moves are given, their effects can be combined rather than memorized as a picture.
Given facts.
Yarrow is 2 map unit(s) north of Dover; Linden is 2 map unit(s) north of Yarrow. A museum in Stone opens on Saturday.
Rules.
Treat east as +x, west as −x, north as +y, and south as −y. Add the moves in order. A fact that does not affect any coordinate is irrelevant.
Task.
Where is Linden relative to Dover? What is the straight grid displacement measured as |x|+|y|? Identify any irrelevant fact.
Step-by-step solution.

1. Start Dover at (0,0). 2. Translate each relation into a coordinate move. 3. Adding the moves gives (0,4). 4. That coordinate is north of Dover; the grid displacement is |0|+|4|=4. 5. The museum sentence changes no coordinate, so it is a distractor.
Answer.
Linden is north of Dover; grid displacement 4 unit(s). The museum fact is irrelevant.
Knowledge takeaway.
Cardinal directions become easier to reason about when they are treated as relations that can be composed.
Formal model.
Grid coordinates; each statement adds a vector; sum the vectors and classify the final coordinate.
